options: I couldn't come because I was sick
I couldn't come in order to be sick
When I was sick, I came
items.explanation: olduğum için means “because I was.” The reason comes first.

items.prompt: Otobüs geç geldiği için geç kaldım.
options: The bus was late so that I'd be late
I was late because the bus came late
I'll be late if the bus is late
items.say: Otobüs geç geldiği için geç kaldım.
items.explanation: geldiği için means because it (the bus) came. Excuse first, then the lateness.

items.prompt: Yarın sınavım olacağı için erken yatıyorum.
options: I go to bed early because the exam was yesterday
I'll go to bed early to pass the exam
I go to bed early because the exam is tomorrow
items.say: Yarın sınavım olacağı için erken yatıyorum.
items.explanation: -acağı için is a reason in the future. The exam is tomorrow.

options: I didn't call because I had no time
I had time, so I called
I'll call when I have time
items.explanation: olmadığı için means because there wasn't. Time is “it,” so -ı.

exercises.instruction: Match the person and the form.

items.explanation: The person hides in the ending: -m, -ı, -miz, -niz. With onlar the k doesn't soften: geldikleri.

items.translation: I was late because I overslept.
items.explanation: kal ends in l, which is voiced, so d. I: -ım.

items.translation: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
items.explanation: ş is voiceless, so d becomes t. The last vowel is ı, so tığım.

items.translation: The match was postponed because it was raining.
items.explanation: Without için you need the formal version: -dığından.

items.translation: I didn't take a taxi because I had no money.
items.explanation: Money is “it,” third person, and there wasn't any: ol + ma + dığı.

exercises.instruction: Build the phrase. The reason goes first.

items.translation: I couldn't come because I was sick.
items.explanation: First the reason with için, then what happened. Çünkü doesn't belong here.

items.translation: The match was postponed because it was raining.
items.explanation: yağdığından is a formal reason, like in the news. It goes first.

exercises.instruction: Paste the right piece into the note. The boss will decide whether to believe it.

items.head: Otobüs geç gel
items.full: Otobüs geç geldiği için geç kaldım.
items.ru: I was late because the bus came late.
items.explanation: The bus came: that's “it,” so -i. After e it's diği.

items.head: Uyuya kal
items.ru: I missed the meeting because I overslept.
items.explanation: I overslept, so -ım. l is voiced, so d.

items.head: Hasta ol
items.ru: I couldn't come because I was sick.
items.explanation: After o comes u: olduğum.

items.head: Yağmur yağ
items.ru: The match was postponed because it was raining.
items.explanation: No için in the note means -dığından. ğ is voiced, so d.

items.head: Yarın erken kalk
items.full: Yarın erken kalkacağım için erken yatıyorum.
items.ru: I go to bed early because I'm getting up early tomorrow.
items.explanation: Tomorrow is a reason in the future, so -acağım.

items.head: Vaktim ol
items.ru: I didn't call because I had no time.
items.explanation: Time is “it,” and there wasn't any: madığı.

exercises.description: A note to the boss: the learner pastes in the right piece of -DIğI / -AcAğI / -DIğIndAn

items.prompt: Geç kaldım çünkü otobüs gelmedi. How do you say it with için?
items.explanation: Reason up front, and the reason's verb is gelmediği. Gelmek için means “in order to come.”

items.statement: -dığından means the same as -dığı için, but sounds more formal.
items.explanation: Yes. Same meaning; -dığından is for the news and letters.
After voiceless t comes t too: gittiğim.

options: I'm learning Turkish because I came to Antalya
I came to Antalya because I learned Turkish
I came to Antalya to learn Turkish
items.explanation: -mak için is a goal: “in order to.” A reason would be öğrendiğim için.
No verb? Call ol-: yorgun olduğum için.
